## Solution

**Step 1: Identify the antiderivative.**

Consider the function $F(x) = x^{xe^x}$. We compute its derivative. Setting $v(x) = xe^x \ln x$, we have $F(x) = e^{v(x)}$, so $F'(x) = x^{xe^x} \cdot v'(x)$.

Now
$$v'(x) = \frac{d}{dx}(xe^x \ln x) = (e^x + xe^x)\ln x + xe^x \cdot \frac{1}{x} = e^x(1+x)\ln x + e^x = e^x\big[(x+1)\ln x + 1\big].$$

Therefore
$$F'(x) = x^{xe^x} \cdot e^x \cdot \big[(x+1)\ln x + 1\big].$$

**Step 2: Rewrite the integrand.**

Observe that
$$e^{x(e^x \ln x + 1)} = e^{xe^x \ln x + x} = e^{xe^x \ln x} \cdot e^x = x^{xe^x} \cdot e^x.$$

Hence the first part of the integrand is exactly $F'(x)$:
$$\big[(x+1)\ln x + 1\big]\, e^{x(e^x \ln x + 1)} = \frac{d}{dx}\!\left[x^{xe^x}\right].$$

**Step 3: Evaluate the integral.**

$$\int_1^{1+1/n}\left\{\big[(x+1)\ln x + 1\big]\, e^{x(e^x \ln x + 1)} + n\right\}dx = \Big[x^{xe^x}\Big]_1^{1+1/n} + n\cdot\frac{1}{n}.$$

At $x=1$: $1^{1\cdot e^1} = 1$. At $x = 1+\tfrac{1}{n}$: $\left(1+\tfrac{1}{n}\right)^{(1+1/n)\,e^{1+1/n}}$.

So the integral equals
$$\left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)^{(1+1/n)\,e^{1+1/n}} - 1 + 1 = \left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)^{(1+1/n)\,e^{1+1/n}}.$$

**Step 4: Compute the limit.**

Set $a_n = \left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)^{(1+1/n)\,e^{1+1/n}}$. We need $\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n^{1/n}$.

$$\ln\!\left(a_n^{1/n}\right) = \frac{1}{n}\ln a_n = \frac{(1+1/n)\,e^{1+1/n}\,\ln(1+1/n)}{n}.$$

As $n \to \infty$:
- $(1+1/n) \to 1$,
- $e^{1+1/n} \to e$,
- $\ln(1+1/n) \sim \frac{1}{n}$.

Therefore
$$\ln\!\left(a_n^{1/n}\right) \sim \frac{1 \cdot e \cdot \frac{1}{n}}{n} = \frac{e}{n^2} \longrightarrow 0.$$

Hence $a_n^{1/n} \to e^0 = 1$.

$$\boxed{\lim_{n \to \infty}\left[\int_1^{1+\frac{1}{n}}\left\{[(x+1)\ln x +1]\, e^{x (e^x \ln x +1)}+n \right\} dx\right]^{\frac{1}{n}} = 1}$$
